title: When the Signal Turns Again
premise: Wren Fairweather, a terraformer tending a garden on the half-dead world of Meridian, spends his runs between the silent colonies carrying seeds and messages no one answers. When a distress signal arrives in Old Terran — extinct for two centuries — he traces it to the Halcyon, a generation ship holding two cryo-banks: one holding the original colonists, one holding a rival faction's chosen few, and power enough to wake only one. Torn between his duty to the terraforming charter and the growing bond he forms with Ilse, a voice from the ship's failing systems who may be a stored consciousness rather than a person, Wren discovers the signal was sent by the ship itself, begging someone to choose. In the end, Wren refuses the binary: he reroutes the terraforming array's power grid to wake both banks slowly, sacrificing the garden and his own cryo-slot, choosing found family over either faction's future.
about_author: Emrys Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former hydrology consultant who traded spreadsheets for starships after a decade mapping water tables on three continents. They write quiet, hopeful science fiction from a converted lighthouse on the Atlantic coast, where the fog does the worldbuilding for them.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. We follow his supply run between Meridian and the silent colony of Ashfall, tending the seed-vault garden meant for future generations, and feel the loneliness of a man serving people not yet born. When the extinct-language signal crackles through his console mid-route, he breaks protocol and answers. Emotional beat: isolation cracked open by the first voice in years.

chapters.title: Two Cradles, One Heartbeat
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, with interleaved fragments of Ilse's transmissions from the Halcyon. Docking with the derelict-adjacent ship, Wren learns of the two cryo-banks and the charter's cold arithmetic: only one can wake. Ilse — warm, funny, possibly not human — helps him map the ship, and he begins to question which 'half of humanity' the word humanity even covers. Emotional beat: duty and desire beginning to pull apart.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Waking
chapters.summary: Alternating Wren and Ilse POVs. The charter's enforcement AI arrives to force the choice, revealing the signal was the ship's own plea — and that waking either bank dooms the garden and Meridian's terraforming. Sabotage, a power failure, and Ilse's confession that she is a stored consciousness slated for deletion push Wren to the edge. Emotional beat: climax — Wren rejects the binary and reroutes the array to wake both banks, burning his own escape.

chapters.title: What the Garden Was For
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, months later. The first sleepers wake to a thinner garden but a larger family; Ilse survives in the ship's grid, her voice now the colony's morning bell. The colonies begin speaking again, and Wren plants a new seed-vault — this time labeled for everyone. Emotional beat: resolution — love and found family chosen over duty's arithmetic, grief transmuted into planting.
